purpose: The installed Syft release (v1.52.0) was previously checksum-verified only (blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/README.md lines 51-52); this check verifies its cosign signature and searches for a build-provenance attestation, and separately widens the local Syft inventory scope onto system interpreter prefixes and native-library directories (results shared with supply-chain-hosted-run-and-wider-syft.json in this same directory, referenced here for gaps 3/9). FIX ROUND CORRECTION (2026-09-23): the original `gh attestation verify` call defaulted to enforcing predicate-type `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1` (SLSA build provenance), and its 404 was mischaracterized as 'no GitHub-native attestation exists' for this asset; the unfiltered `gh api repos/anchore/syft/attestations/sha256:...` endpoint returns a GitHub-native release attestation (predicateType release/v0.2), and `gh release verify-asset` verifies it successfully. This revision corrects that finding using the procedure the review identified as the right one (predicate-type-aware verification), run once with a new preregistration; it does not re-run the original 404 check to get a different outcome.
preregistered: If `cosign verify-blob` against Syft's published checksums file, using its keyless certificate and signature, returns 'Verified OK', that settles the signature half of gaps 3 and 9 in the supports_incumbent direction. `gh attestation verify` against the syft release tarball's exact digest either finds and verifies a build-provenance attestation (further supporting the incumbent) or returns a real 404 (an honest negative result, recorded as-is, not retried against a different digest or repo to fish for a match). The wider-scan half is preregistered jointly with supply-chain-hosted-run-and-wider-syft.json: either it finds materially more/less inventory outside the single-prefix baseline, or it demonstrates a structural blind spot.

commands.cmd: curl -sSL -o cosign-linux-amd64 https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v2.6.1/cosign-linux-amd64 && curl -sSL -o cosign_checksums.txt https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v2.6.1/cosign_checksums.txt && grep cosign-linux-amd64$ cosign_checksums.txt | awk '{print $1}' > expected.txt && sha256sum cosign-linux-amd64 | awk '{print $1}' > actual.txt && diff expected.txt actual.txt
commands.output_excerpt: 064954c5d8c7e3b28188eee5b1727b31c411550bc5fefd41aa672d3c761d103a matches for both files; diff produced no output (checksum match)

commands.cmd: cosign verify-blob --certificate cosign_checksums.txt-keyless.pem --signature cosign_checksums.txt-keyless.sig --certificate-identity keyless@projectsigstore.iam.gserviceaccount.com --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com cosign_checksums.txt

curl -sSL -o syft_1.52.0_checksums.txt(.pem/.sig) [the syft release's own checksums file plus its cosign signature/certificate assets] && cosign verify-blob --certificate syft_1.52.0_checksums.txt.pem --signature syft_1.52.0_checksums.txt.sig --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github\.com/anchore/syft/\.github/workflows/.*\.ya?ml.*' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com syft_1.52.0_checksums.txt

curl -sSL -o syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz https://github.com/anchore/syft/releases/download/v1.52.0/syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz && sha256sum syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz && tar -xzf syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz syft -O | sha256sum && sha256sum $(readlink -f $(which syft))

result: Installed cosign v2.6.1 into a new prefix, checksum-verified against its own published checksums file. Used it to verify (a) the cosign_checksums.txt file's own keyless Sigstore signature (Verified OK, signer keyless@projectsigstore.iam.gserviceaccount.com via accounts.google.com -- this is cosign's own release-signing identity, the expected bootstrap-trust anchor for the cosign release itself), and (b) Syft v1.52.0's checksums file signature (Verified OK, signer identity matched the regex for anchore/syft's own GitHub Actions release workflow via token.actions.githubusercontent.com). The syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz tarball's sha256 matched the now-signature-verified checksums file exactly, and extracting it reproduced the exact bytes of the already-installed syft binary (15a52d01...) -- so the previously checksum-only-verified install is now also signature-chain-verified back to anchore/syft's release workflow identity. FIX ROUND CORRECTION: `gh attestation verify` against the syft tarball's exact digest returned a real HTTP 404, but that call implicitly enforces predicate-type https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 (gh attestation verify's documented default) -- it is a 404 for SLSA build provenance specifically, not evidence of 'no GitHub-native attestation'. The unfiltered `gh api repos/anchore/syft/attestations/sha256:<digest>` endpoint DOES return an attestation for this exact digest: a GitHub-native immutable-release attestation (predicateType https://in-toto.io/attestation/release/v0.2, signer identity https://dotcom.releases.github.com, a GitHub-operated, not anchore/syft-operated, signer -- this is GitHub's platform-level 'this asset really is attached to this release' attestation, distinct in kind from a repo-workflow-signed SLSA build-provenance attestation). `gh release verify-asset v1.52.0 syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz --repo anchore/syft` (the command purpose-built for this predicate type) succeeded: 'Verification succeeded! syft_1.52.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz is present in release v1.52.0'. So a GitHub-native attestation for this exact asset digest does exist and does verify; anchore/syft's tarball has both a verified cosign/Sigstore blob signature (workflow-identity-signed) and a verified GitHub-native release attestation (GitHub-platform-signed) -- two independent, both-passing provenance mechanisms, not one present and one absent. Wider local-scan results for external interpreters and native libraries are recorded in supply-chain-hosted-run-and-wider-syft.json in this same directory, including its own fix-round correction (61 packages found in /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages; the earlier 'only 4 of many native libraries attributed' claim for /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu is corrected there to a scan-scoping artifact, not a Syft blind spot -- see that receipt).

verdict_impact.explanation: Signature verification (the specific missing check named in both gap texts) is now done and passed for the installed Syft release, closing that half of gaps 3 and 9 with native_proven evidence, and is now further supported by an independently verified GitHub-native release attestation for the exact same asset digest (found via unfiltered gh api and verified via gh release verify-asset), which the original run's gh attestation verify call did not surface because it enforces a different predicate type by default. This strengthens, not weakens, the incumbent's provenance posture for gaps 3/9: two independent, passing provenance checks exist for this release asset. The wider-scan half remains only partially settled and its native-library-completeness claim is now recorded as inconclusive in supply-chain-hosted-run-and-wider-syft.json, not supports_incumbent.

limitations: cosign was installed fresh into a new prefix for this check and used without independently verifying cosign's own release binary against a build-provenance attestation (a bootstrap-trust question: the checksum match plus the fact that cosign's checksums.txt itself carries a valid keyless signature from cosign's known release identity is the trust basis used here, consistent with the sigstore project's own documented verification model, but this is not a third, independent root of trust).

The GitHub-native release attestation (predicateType release/v0.2) proves this asset is attached to anchore/syft's v1.52.0 GitHub release and is signed by GitHub's own release-attestation identity (dotcom.releases.github.com); it is not a SLSA build-provenance attestation and does not by itself prove which anchore/syft workflow run produced the binary bytes -- that stronger claim is instead supported by the separately verified cosign/Sigstore signature, whose signer identity is scoped to anchore/syft's own release workflow.

See supply-chain-hosted-run-and-wider-syft.json's limitations for the wider-scan portion (full /usr/lib scan incomplete; native-library coverage measured on one subdirectory only, and the earlier low-attribution claim there is now corrected to inconclusive rather than a demonstrated Syft limitation).
